uncited: DropGaussian modifies the standard 3DGS training loop by introducing a stochastic dropout mechanism applied to the Gaussian primitives.

*   Set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G} = \{g_i\}$, where each $g_i$ contains position $\mathbf{p}_i$, scale $\mathbf{s}_i$, rotation $\mathbf{q}_i$, opacity $o_i$, and spherical harmonic coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i$.
*   Current training iteration index $t$.
*   Total number of training iterations $t_{\text{total}}$.
*   Base dropping rate parameter $r$ (typically 0.1).
*   Scaling factor $\gamma$ (typically 1).
*   Target training view image $I_{\text{target}}$.
*   Rendered image $I_{\text{rendered}}$ using the modified Gaussian set.
*   Gradients backpropagated only to the non-dropped Gaussians.
The method operates on the standard 3DGS primitive representation defined in the parent article [Pruning and Density Control](16215-pruning-and-density-control.md).
No new data structures are introduced; the method modifies the opacity values $o_i$ temporarily during the forward pass.
Represents the fraction of Gaussians to remove.
A binary mask $M(i)$ is determined based on whether the Gaussian is dropped.
**Select Gaussians to Drop:** Randomly select a subset of Gaussians to be dropped.
The selection probability for each Gaussian should correspond to $r_t$.
*   If $i$ is selected to be dropped, set its effective opacity contribution to 0 (effectively removing it from rendering).
**Backpropagate:** Compute gradients of $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to the Gaussian parameters.
The progressive schedule $r_t$ addresses this by starting with a low or zero drop rate and increasing it over time.
Manages the growth curve of primitives, synchronizing densification with rendering resolution.
DropGaussian complements this by controlling overfitting during the densified phase. [Link](15107-optimization-schedule-and-densification.md)
Uses reconstruction error to guide pruning.
DropGaussian differs by using random structural regularization rather than error-based pruning. [Link](16199-reconstruction-aware-pruning-scheduler.md)
*   **Time Complexity**: The method adds negligible computational overhead.
It involves a simple random selection and opacity scaling, which are $O(N)$ operations where $N$ is the number of Gaussians.
*   **Memory Complexity**: No additional memory is required beyond the standard 3DGS representation.
*   **Strengths**: Prior-free, no external data required, simple implementation, effective against overfitting in sparse views.
May not be as effective in dense-view settings where overfitting is less of an issue.
*   **When to use**: Sparse-view novel view synthesis where overfitting to training views is a concern.
*   **When not to use**: Dense-view settings where standard 3DGS performs well, or when external priors are available and preferred.
The method addresses the limitation of standard 3DGS in sparse-view settings, where it tends to overfit to the limited number of training views.
